rationale: The candidate is coherent enough to read in all four views, but it is still fundamentally a compact two-tiered box with a mild bend rather than a neighborhood-building massing. The curved top helps the silhouette, yet the form does not establish a strong dominant gesture or a convincing public void. The verified road frontage/access edge is not answered by a legible undercut, court, or entry seam; the frontage remains semantically muted. Relative to the references, it borrows the general low-rise/courtyard family but misses the clearer open-space hierarchy and active ground condition that define the program. It is not a hard typology mismatch, but it is not program-fit enough to pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and materially refined; candidate is much more compact and box-dominant.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise composed massing with a carved central void and a bridge-like upper connector can support neighborhood program well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate does not have the multi-volume richness or distributed hierarchy of the reference.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a public court can create legible open-space hierarchy for mixed neighborhood use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more horizontally spread and porous; candidate reads too compact and enclosed.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise body with a clear void and a slightly folded roof language helps neighborhood-scale public program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate lacks a convincing terrace/courtyard section relationship and feels more like a stacked block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced or stepped continuity around a public open space can create a stable neighborhood massing figure.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate has only a weak threshold articulation and does not resolve the ground as a public figure.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with voids under elevated masses can produce a clear public threshold and hierarchy.
